title: Persuading
job: Make a case, concede a point, hold your ground
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedPatterns: Einerseits + V-2 + ich + , + andererseits + V-2 + ich
Ich komme nicht + , + ich habe nämlich keine Zeit

rules.text: THE FIRST POSITION IS AN ARGUMENTATIVE CHOICE. German allows exactly one element before the finite verb, and by now you have met that as a mechanical law five times. Here it is a tool: what you FRONT is what you are arguing from. Sort the connectives once, on three classes the course already owns — obwohl and weil send the verb LAST (L3-M3, L1-M9); aber and denn leave it SECOND and count as nothing at all; trotzdem and deshalb FRONT and invert (L3-M3, L1-M9). This module's four join the third class: außerdem, dennoch, einerseits, andererseits.

ZWAR IS NOT ADMITTEDLY. English admittedly is a whole adverb standing apart from its clause; zwar stands INSIDE the clause it concedes and belongs to it, usually straight after the verb: Das ist zwar teuer, aber … . It never stands alone, it never opens a sentence on its own, and the aber half always follows — a zwar with nothing after it is half a sentence.

NÄMLICH HAS NO ENGLISH COUNTERPART. It gives the reason AFTER the claim, it never stands first, it takes no comma of its own, and it sits in the middle field: Ich komme nicht mit, ich habe nämlich keine Zeit. Set it against the two you already own on the same pair of facts: weil builds a subordinate clause with the verb LAST, denn builds a main clause with the verb SECOND, and nämlich builds no clause at all — it simply marks the sentence it is in as the explanation of the one before.

EINERSEITS … ANDERERSEITS INVERT, EVERY TIME. English on the one hand / on the other hand leaves the sentence alone: on the one hand IT IS expensive. Both German halves are single elements in first position, so the finite verb follows immediately and the subject comes after it: Einerseits IST das teuer, andererseits IST es sehr gut. Forgetting the inversion is the mistake that survives longest, because the English shape reads as grammatical until you say it aloud.

EVENTUELL IS THE FALSE FRIEND THIS MODULE WOULD OTHERWISE MINT. eventuell means possibly, not eventually — English eventually is schließlich, which is L2-M10's. It is named here and deliberately not written, because a hedge belongs to L4-M5 next door and a word this treacherous deserves its own row rather than a corner of one. The other one is already settled: also means therefore and never English also, which is auch, and L1-M10 owns both words.

WHAT A CASE ALREADY HAS, so nothing here is re-minted. weil, denn, deshalb, dass, warum, finde, glaube, denke are L1-M9's. aber, oder, und, dann, also are L1-M10's. obwohl, trotzdem, Meinung, stimmt, Recht, sicher, natürlich, ehrlich, wirklich, Grund are L3-M3's — most of a persuasion vocabulary paid for already. Es geht darum, dass … is L4-M2's da-compound earning its keep one module later, and it points back there. Softening and hedging are NOT this module's job: they are L4-M5's, one rung on. This module makes the case and holds the ground.

sentences.display: Das ist zwar teuer, aber es ist wirklich gut
sentences.cue: That is expensive, admittedly, but it is really good
sentences.literal: That is admittedly expensive, but it is really good

words.note: zwar concedes from INSIDE its clause, straight after the verb, and always has an aber half behind it. It never stands alone.

sentences.trap: zwar is not a first-position word. Das zwar ist teuer and Zwar, das ist teuer are both wrong: it sits after the finite verb, in the middle field.
sentences.sound: das ist tsvaar TOY-er, AA-ber es ist VIRK-likh GOOT.

variations.display: Der Termin ist zwar am Montag, aber ich komme trotzdem
variations.cue: The appointment is on Monday, admittedly, but I am coming anyway
variations.changed: The same concession on a different fact, and trotzdem (L3-M3) closes it — a fronting connective, so the verb follows it.

mistake.display: Zwar das ist teuer, aber es ist wirklich gut
mistake.why: zwar does not take first position. Put it after the finite verb, inside the clause it concedes: Das ist zwar teuer.

sentences.usage: Granting the obvious objection before you make your point.
sentences.mnemonic: zwar sits down inside its clause; aber does the standing up.

sentences.display: Einerseits ist das teuer, andererseits ist es sehr gut
sentences.cue: On the one hand that is expensive, on the other it is very good
sentences.literal: One-side is that expensive, other-side is it very good

words.note: One element in first position, so the verb follows it at once: Einerseits ist das teuer. It expects an andererseits behind it.
The answering half, and it inverts exactly the same way: andererseits ist es sehr gut. Three e's in a row is the spelling learners drop.

sentences.trap: English on the one hand moves nothing. Both German halves are fronted elements, so the verb comes second and the subject third — every time, in both halves.
sentences.sound: AI-ner-zaits ist das TOY-er, AN-der-er-zaits ist es zair GOOT.

variations.display: Einerseits habe ich Zeit, andererseits habe ich kein Geld
variations.cue: On the one hand I have time, on the other I have no money
variations.changed: Both halves keep the inversion with a different verb: habe ich, not ich habe.

mistake.display: Einerseits das ist teuer, andererseits es ist sehr gut
mistake.why: Both connectives occupy first position, so the finite verb must be second: Einerseits ist das teuer, andererseits ist es sehr gut.

sentences.usage: Weighing two sides out loud before you land on one.
sentences.mnemonic: Two hands, two inversions — the verb shakes first each time.

sentences.display: Ich komme nicht mit, ich habe nämlich keine Zeit
sentences.cue: I am not coming along; I have no time, you see
sentences.literal: I come not along, I have namely no time

words.note: Explains the sentence before it, from inside the middle field. It never stands first and takes no comma of its own.

sentences.trap: nämlich builds no clause. weil would send the verb last and denn would open a second main clause; nämlich changes nothing about word order at all.
sentences.sound: ikh KOM-uh nikht MIT, ikh HAA-buh NAIM-likh KAI-nuh TSAIT.

variations.display: Ich komme nicht mit, denn ich habe keine Zeit
variations.cue: I am not coming along, because I have no time
variations.changed: denn (L1-M9) says the same thing as a conjunction and stands between the clauses; nämlich lives inside the second one.

mistake.why: nämlich cannot open a sentence — it is not a connective at all, only a marker inside one. Use denn or weil to open, or move nämlich behind the verb.

sentences.usage: Adding the reason as an afterthought, once the claim has landed.
sentences.mnemonic: nämlich never leads; it explains from the middle of the room.

sentences.display: Außerdem ist der Termin schon am Montag
sentences.cue: Besides, the appointment is already on Monday
sentences.literal: Besides is the appointment already on Monday

words.note: Adds a second argument and fronts, so the verb follows it: Außerdem ist der Termin am Montag. The ß is written, never a double s.

sentences.trap: English besides and what is more leave the sentence standing. außerdem is a fronted element, so the finite verb comes straight after it.
sentences.sound: OW-ser-daym ist dair ter-MEEN shohn am MOHN-taag.

variations.display: Außerdem habe ich am Montag keine Zeit
variations.cue: Besides, I have no time on Monday
variations.changed: A different verb after the same fronted connective; ich still lands behind it.

mistake.display: Außerdem der Termin ist schon am Montag
mistake.why: außerdem holds first position, so the verb takes second: Außerdem ist der Termin schon am Montag.

sentences.usage: Stacking a second reason on top of the first.
sentences.mnemonic: außerdem steps in front, and the verb steps up behind it.

sentences.display: Es geht darum, dass wir eine Lösung finden
sentences.cue: The point is that we find a solution
sentences.literal: It goes there-about, that we a solution find

words.cue: it is about, the point is
words.note: A fixed pair with darum: Es geht darum, dass … . Nothing here is about going — es geht um means the matter at hand.
die Lösung, from lösen, to solve or to loosen. eine Lösung finden is the pair German uses where English reaches a solution.

sentences.trap: darum is L4-M2's da-word doing its anticipating job: it holds the place of the dass-clause hanging behind it, and the dass-clause is verb-final as ever.
sentences.sound: es gayt da-RUM, das veer AI-nuh LOE-zung FIN-dun.

variations.display: Es geht darum, dass wir zusammen eine Antwort finden
variations.cue: The point is that we find an answer together
variations.changed: The dass-clause grows a word and finden stays where it was — at the very end.

mistake.display: Es geht darum, dass wir finden eine Lösung
mistake.why: dass is subordinating, so its verb goes to the end: dass wir eine Lösung finden. The da-word in front changes nothing about that.

sentences.usage: Pulling a wandering discussion back to what is actually at stake.
sentences.mnemonic: Es geht darum — the placeholder points, the dass-clause answers.

sentences.display: Das ist ein guter Vorschlag, aber ich habe eine Frage
sentences.cue: That is a good suggestion, but I have a question
sentences.literal: That is a good suggestion, but I have a question

words.note: der Vorschlag, from vorschlagen — literally to strike something forward. einen Vorschlag machen is the pair for making one.

sentences.trap: aber counts as nothing in the count to position two, so the clause behind it starts over: aber ICH HABE, not aber habe ich.
sentences.sound: das ist ain GOO-ter FOR-shlaag, AA-ber ikh HAA-buh AI-nuh FRAA-guh.

variations.display: Das ist ein guter Vorschlag, aber er ist zu teuer
variations.cue: That is a good suggestion, but it is too expensive
variations.changed: er picks up der Vorschlag — masculine, so er and not es.

mistake.display: Das ist ein guter Vorschlag, aber habe ich eine Frage
mistake.why: aber is one of the connectives that count as nothing. The clause after it is an ordinary main clause: aber ich habe eine Frage.

sentences.usage: Conceding the shape of a plan before you question a part of it.
sentences.mnemonic: aber is a doorway, not a step — the clause walks in unchanged.

sentences.display: Ihr Argument ist gut, dennoch bin ich dagegen
sentences.cue: Your argument is good; even so, I am against it
sentences.literal: Your argument is good, nevertheless am I against-it

words.cue: argument, a point in a case
words.note: das Argument is a point you make, never a quarrel. A quarrel is der Streit — this word only ever means the reasoning.
The bookish twin of trotzdem (L3-M3), and it fronts and inverts the same way: dennoch bin ich dagegen.
L4-M2's da-compound again: gegen plus a thing becomes dagegen. Against a person stays gegen ihn — a da-word never stands for somebody.

sentences.trap: Ihr keeps its capital. Lowercase ihr would be her or their, and the index cannot see the difference — the capital is the only signal your reader gets.
sentences.sound: eer ar-goo-MENT ist GOOT, DEN-okh bin ikh da-GAY-gun.

variations.display: Ihr Argument ist gut, trotzdem bin ich dagegen
variations.cue: Your argument is good; all the same, I am against it
variations.changed: trotzdem for dennoch — the everyday twin. Both front, so bin ich stays inverted either way.

mistake.display: Ihr Argument ist gut, dennoch ich bin dagegen
mistake.why: dennoch takes first position in its own clause, so the verb is second: dennoch bin ich dagegen.

sentences.usage: Holding your ground after granting the other side its due.
sentences.mnemonic: dennoch fronts, bin follows, ich waits — the ground is held.

sentences.display: Der Punkt überzeugt mich überhaupt nicht
sentences.cue: That point does not convince me at all
sentences.literal: The point convinces me at-all not

words.note: der Punkt is a point in a case and also a full stop. Say der Punkt or dieser Punkt; mein Punkt is an English shape German avoids.
überzeugen takes an accusative person: es überzeugt mich. Ich bin überzeugt is the state that results.
Sharpens a negative and comes just before nicht: überhaupt nicht is not at all. On its own in a question it means anyway, at all.

sentences.trap: meinen Punkt does not work: meinen is L2-M8's verb, to mean. Say der Punkt or dieser Punkt and the sentence stays yours.
sentences.sound: dair PUNKT ue-ber-TSOYKT mikh ue-ber-HOWPT nikht.

variations.display: Der Punkt überzeugt mich wirklich nicht
variations.cue: That point really does not convince me
variations.changed: wirklich (L3-M3) for überhaupt: the same seat in front of nicht, one degree softer.

mistake.display: Der Punkt überzeugt mich nicht überhaupt
mistake.why: überhaupt leans on the negative from in front of it, never behind: überhaupt nicht. Reversed, it reads as two separate words with no force.

sentences.usage: Rejecting an argument squarely, without rejecting the person.
sentences.mnemonic: überhaupt nicht — the intensifier walks in front of the no.

sentences.display: Wir müssen das unbedingt heute besprechen
sentences.cue: We absolutely have to discuss that today
sentences.literal: We must that unconditionally today discuss

words.note: Literally uncondition-ed: no conditions attached. It strengthens a demand and sits in the middle field, before the time word.
etwas besprechen takes a plain accusative — no preposition. sprechen über exists too; besprechen is the one that means settle it between us.

sentences.trap: unbedingt is not a time word and does not front here. It belongs in the middle field, and the infinitive besprechen still closes the clause.
sentences.sound: veer MUES-un das UN-be-dingt HOY-tuh buh-SHPREKH-un.

variations.display: Wir müssen das unbedingt am Montag besprechen
variations.cue: We absolutely have to discuss that on Monday
variations.changed: The time phrase grows; unbedingt keeps its seat in front of it and besprechen keeps the last.

mistake.display: Wir müssen unbedingt besprechen das heute
mistake.why: The modal sends besprechen to the end, and everything else lines up in front of it: das unbedingt heute besprechen.

sentences.usage: Pressing for a decision without raising your voice.
sentences.mnemonic: unbedingt — no conditions, and no moving to the front either.

sentences.display: Das ist keine gute Idee, denn es ist zu teuer
sentences.cue: That is not a good idea, because it is too expensive
sentences.literal: That is no good idea, because it is too expensive

words.note: die Idee, stressed on the last syllable: ee-DAY. The plural adds an n — die Ideen — and is pronounced with both e's.
gut takes -e in front of a feminine noun after eine or keine: eine gute Idee. The masculine form guter is L3-M2's.

sentences.trap: denn leaves the word order alone: denn ES IST zu teuer. weil would send it to the end — weil es zu teuer IST — and both are correct German for the same fact.
sentences.sound: das ist KAI-nuh GOO-tuh ee-DAY, den es ist tsoo TOY-er.

variations.display: Das ist keine gute Idee, weil es zu teuer ist
variations.cue: That is not a good idea, because it is too expensive
variations.changed: weil for denn, and the verb drops to the end of its clause. The meaning does not move an inch.

mistake.display: Das ist keine gute Idee, denn es zu teuer ist
mistake.why: denn is a coordinating conjunction and counts as nothing: the clause behind it keeps its verb in second place. Only weil moves it to the end.

sentences.usage: Turning down a proposal and paying for the refusal with a reason.
sentences.mnemonic: denn leaves the furniture where it is; weil rearranges the room.
